    # More elaborate tests done in test_masked.py
    @classmethod

        self.ma = Masked(np.arange(3), mask=[True, False, False])

        out0 = np.array2string(self.ma)
        assert out0 == '[— 1 2]'
        # Arguments are interpreted as usual.
        out1 = np.array2string(self.ma, separator=', ')

        assert out3 == out2
        # But not if the formatter is not relevant for us.
        out4 = np.array2string(self.ma, separator=', ', formatter={'float': hex})

        ma2 = self.ma.astype('f4')

generates new subclasses for any data class that is itself a

"""Regression tests for printing masked structured arrays with subarrays."""

import numpy as np
import pytest

from astropy.utils.masked import Masked


@pytest.mark.parametrize('shape', [(), (2,), (2, 2)])
@pytest.mark.parametrize('dtype', [
    [('value', 'i4', (2,))],
    [('value', 'i4', (2, 2))],
    [('record', [('value', 'i4', (2,))])],
    [('records', [('value', 'i4')], (2,))],
])
def test_array2string_structured_subarrays(dtype, shape):
    data = np.ones(shape, dtype=dtype)
    masked = Masked(data, mask=False)
    expected = np.array2string(data)
    assert np.array2string(masked) == expected
    assert str(masked) == str(data)
    with np.printoptions(linewidth=1000):
        assert repr(masked) == repr(data).replace('array(', 'MaskedNDArray(', 1)
    # Fully masked fields should preserve the structure and punctuation.
    masked.mask = True
    assert np.array2string(masked) == expected.replace('1', '—')
